capability_investigated:
processor() feature-extraction shape and generate()'s batch dimension —
whether features can carry multiple 30s windows and whether generate accepts
one prompt per window and returns a per-window result list.
what_i_learned:
The default processor(audio) emits input_features of shape [1, n_mels, 3000]
i.e. a single 30s window — anything past 30s is truncated and lost. generate
takes a batched features StorageView and a prompts list aligned to the batch,
returning one result per window, so long-form audio can be covered by
self-windowing rather than the truncated single call.
hypothesis:
Split audio into consecutive 30s windows, feature-extract each, concatenate
into one batched StorageView, decode all in a single batched generate call
with one prompt per window, and join the texts. This recovers the deleted
tail of every multi-minute 0715 call, which should sharply cut deletion-driven
CER versus the 30s-only stub.

capability_investigated:
generate()'s batch dimension and GPU memory cost — specifically whether the
OOM in iter 1 came from batching every 30s window's features into a single
generate() StorageView, versus decoding windows one at a time.
what_i_learned:
Batching all windows of a multi-minute call into one generate() call scales
GPU memory with the window count and OOMs on long 0715 calls. generate()
decodes correctly with a batch-of-1 features view and a single-element prompt
list, so windows can be processed sequentially at bounded (one-window) peak
memory while still covering the full audio — no truncation, no OOM.
hypothesis:
Keep iter 1's full-audio self-windowing (fixes structural tail-deletion) but
decode each 30s window in its own batch-of-1 generate() call and join the
texts, so the pipeline actually runs to completion instead of crashing.

capability_investigated:
generate()'s returned sequences_ids when <|notimestamps|> is removed from the
prompt — i.e. whether the decoder emits timestamp tokens and what they encode
about how much of each 30s window the model consumed.
what_i_learned:
Without <|notimestamps|> the decode emits timestamp tokens (ids >= the
<|0.00|> token id) interleaved with text tokens in sequences_ids. The last
such token gives the chunk-relative time (steps * 0.02s) the model accounted
for, so the window can advance to a model-chosen boundary instead of a fixed
30s cut. This is a return value we were throwing away by forcing notimestamps.
hypothesis:
Replace blind non-overlapping 30s stepping with timestamp-driven adaptive
seek: decode each window with timestamps on, append the text tokens (filtered
below timestamp_begin), and advance seek by the last emitted timestamp
(capped at chunk length, floored at 1s for progress). Utterances split across
hard 30s boundaries should be recovered, lifting length_ratio and cutting the
dominant deletion mass.

capability_investigated:
Re-examined the failure mode of the frozen backend import path: the iter 3
traceback crashes at frozen/asr_backend.py `import ctranslate2` with
`GLIBCXX_3.4.32 not found`, i.e. before transcribe() executes. Also revisited
the window-stride arithmetic in the known-good iter 2 generate() loop.
what_i_learned:
The iter 3 failure was NOT in workspace/transcribe.py — it is an environment
ImportError raised at module load of frozen.asr_backend (libstdc++/GLIBCXX
mismatch), which would crash any transcribe.py identically and cannot be
fixed from the workspace. The timestamp-seek logic therefore never ran and is
unverified. The fixed 30s window cut clips utterances straddling a boundary,
a deletion source that pure stride overlap addresses without any timestamp
decoding.
hypothesis:
Fall back to the known-good iter 2 sequential-window pipeline (notimestamps,
batch-of-1) to guarantee a runnable scoring candidate, and overlap windows by
2s (stride = 28s) so boundary-straddling speech is fully contained in at least
one window, recovering some of the 35% missing content (length_ratio 0.65,
del 80%) with a change that is pure arithmetic and cannot reintroduce a crash.

capability_investigated:
Not a backend decode capability this time but the frozen import path itself:
the GLIBCXX_3.4.32 ImportError raised at `import ctranslate2` inside
frozen.asr_backend before transcribe() runs, and whether it is resolvable
from workspace via ctypes-level dynamic-loader control rather than via the
backend API.
what_i_learned:
The iter-4 ledger claim "unfixable from the workspace" is incomplete. The
crash is a symbol-resolution failure: anaconda's bundled libstdc++.so.6 lacks
the GLIBCXX_3.4.32 version node that libctranslate2.so.4 requires, while the
system libstdc++ provides it. dlopen-ing the newer system libstdc++ with
RTLD_GLOBAL before numpy/frozen pull anaconda's copy in adds the missing
version node to global scope, so ctranslate2 can load — addressable purely
from workspace/transcribe.py with ctypes (no backend/ctranslate2 import).
hypothesis:
Adding a best-effort _preload_libstdcxx() shim at module top, before
importing numpy and frozen.asr_backend, lets the previously-crashing import
succeed, so the known-good iter-2 sequential-window pipeline (cer 0.4087)
actually scores instead of dying at import. Decode body unchanged; shim is
no-op when no newer lib exists, so it cannot regress the import.

capability_investigated:
generate()'s **decoding_kwargs surface — specifically the
no_repeat_ngram_size constraint, which the current greedy decode call
(beam_size=1, sampling_temperature=0.0) never passes. Examined how
ctranslate2.models.Whisper.generate applies n-gram repetition blocking
during decoding, as opposed to the beam/temperature scalars already swept.
what_i_learned:
no_repeat_ngram_size is an accepted decode kwarg distinct from any tried
knob: it is a structural decode-time constraint (forbid re-emitting any
n-gram), not a continuous scalar. This is the lever for the repetition-
collapse failure mode — the repeated_text flag (0.27 corpus, length_ratio
0.32 on the 233s-monologue focus file) indicates the greedy decoder loops
on a phrase then terminates the 30s window early, converting the remaining
speech into deletion (the 80% del axis). The knob attacks deletion via the
repetition mechanism, not via a coverage scalar.
hypothesis:
Add no_repeat_ngram_size=4 to the per-window generate call. Breaking exact
4-gram loops should stop the decoder from stalling and abandoning the rest
of a window, letting it continue to real unseen content — directly raising
length_ratio on the repeated_text files while leaving natural sub-4-token
Korean repeats (네 네, 예 예) untouched.

capability_investigated:
Not a decode kwarg this iter but the module-load path: the
`from frozen.asr_backend import ...` line that triggers `import ctranslate2`,
and whether the system libstdc++ providing GLIBCXX_3.4.32 can be forced into
global symbol scope from workspace via ctypes before anaconda's copy loads.
what_i_learned:
The system libstdc++ is concretely at
/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libstdc++.so.6.0.33 (soname libstdc++.so.6); it
carries the GLIBCXX_3.4.32 node that anaconda's bundled copy lacks. Doing
ctypes.CDLL(that_path, mode=RTLD_GLOBAL) at the very top of transcribe.py —
strictly before the frozen import — puts the missing version node in global
scope so frozen.asr_backend's `import ctranslate2` resolves. The fix must
precede the frozen import line; placing it after (or omitting it) reproduces
the iters 3-6 evaluator crash identically since the failure is at module load.
hypothesis:
iters 3-6 all died at `import ctranslate2` (GLIBCXX_3.4.32 not found), not in
transcribe() logic, so no candidate could score. Preloading the system
libstdc++ with RTLD_GLOBAL before the frozen import resolves the symbol while
leaving the best (iter_002) windowing/sequential-decode pipeline untouched —
the minimal repair that lets the pipeline actually run and bank its gains.

capability_investigated:
The frozen module-load path, not a decode kwarg: why iter 7's
ctypes.CDLL(system libstdc++, RTLD_GLOBAL) preload — placed before the
`from frozen.asr_backend import ...` line — still crashed the evaluator at
`import ctranslate2` with the same GLIBCXX_3.4.32 ImportError.
what_i_learned:
The workspace-side libstdc++ preload CANNOT work, settling the iters 5-7
optimism. anaconda's libstdc++.so.6 is already RESIDENT in the process
before workspace/transcribe.py is imported (evaluate.py / numpy pull it in
first), and dlopen of a different path sharing the same soname
(libstdc++.so.6) returns the already-loaded object — it does NOT inject the
missing GLIBCXX_3.4.32 version node into global scope. So the preload is a
no-op and ctranslate2 still resolves against anaconda's older copy. The
iter-4 conclusion stands: this is an environment fault fixable only before
the process starts (LD_PRELOAD), never from inside the workspace module.
hypothesis:
Stop fighting the unfixable env: revert to the runnable iter-2 windowing
best (drop the ctypes block entirely) so a real score is possible whenever
the env is healthy, and add one zero-risk post-process guard — skip
appending a window whose decoded text exactly equals the previous window's
text — to trim the cross-window face of the repeated_text flag without any
decode-kwarg or env dependency.

capability_investigated:
generate()'s **decoding_kwargs surface — specifically repetition_penalty,
the continuous logit-penalty knob the frozen backend docstring lists
alongside length_penalty/sampling_*. The current greedy call (beam_size=1,
sampling_temperature=0.0) passes neither it nor any repetition control.
what_i_learned:
repetition_penalty is a distinct accepted decode kwarg from
no_repeat_ngram_size (iter_006): it is a soft, continuous multiplicative
penalty on already-emitted token logits, not a hard structural n-gram ban.
It is the untried soft lever for the repeated_text failure mode, where the
greedy decoder loops on a phrase and terminates the 30s window early —
truncating the window tail into the dominant 80% deletion / length_ratio
0.65 axis. (Also confirmed from the ledger: the iter-8 import crash is an
environment GLIBCXX fault at frozen module load, NOT a transcribe.py bug, so
the correct repair is to restore the iter_002 base and drop the unverified
dedup rather than chase the loader.)
hypothesis:
Starting from the known-good iter_002 windowed batch-of-1 pipeline (the only
form that scored, 0.4087), add repetition_penalty=1.1 to each window's
generate() call. By discouraging the greedy phrase-loop that collapses a
window, more of the window's later speech is decoded before EOS, raising
per-window length_ratio and recovering deletion on the repeated_text files
without the duplication risk of overlap or the rejected adjacent dedup.

capability_investigated:
The window-stride arithmetic feeding processor()/generate(), not a new decode
kwarg: how the fixed 30s hop in the iter_002 loop slices audio and what
happens to an utterance straddling a chunk boundary.
what_i_learned:
The iter_002 loop hops by exactly the full 30s window (range(0,n,window)), so
every chunk boundary is a hard cut: an utterance spanning the boundary is
split with no acoustic context on either side, a within-coverage deletion
source distinct from tail truncation (already fixed) and from repetition
collapse. The processor accepts a sub-30s overlapped chunk identically, and a
hop < window simply re-decodes the seam region — recoverable by trimming the
duplicated word-prefix at the join rather than by any backend capability.
hypothesis:
Hop by (window - 2s) instead of the full window and trim the doubled overlap
via a word-suffix/prefix dedup join. The previous attempt's repetition_penalty
never ran (environmental GLIBCXX crash at frozen import, unfixable from
workspace per ledger iters 4/8), so this repair restores the scoring iter_002
base and attacks the deletion axis structurally instead of re-submitting the
crashed kwarg.
